mathematicalAssessment: The population [0,n) is finite for each nonnegative integer n, with arbitrary size and no fixed bound. This is an unbounded-size family of finite populations, not an infinite-population model.

The chooser is a relational definition: inside population, active transformed occurrence, no active withholding, no conflicting active transform identities, and no earlier active transform. Membership/firstness and several safety results are definitional consequences; uniqueness additionally uses integer total order. These are correct conditional algebraic properties, not evidence that an implementation computes that relation.

The alternate population uses point updates If(x==j,replacement,original) for kind and identity while eligibility and population size remain fixed and j is inactive. This represents an arbitrary metadata change at exactly one inactive position. Contributor-set equivalence quantifies positions and kinds. The two selected-occurrence implications together establish equivalence, without assuming both chooser outcomes in the premises.

All 14 theorem premises are independently satisfiable. The corrected invariance controls distinguish the active-filter omission demonstrated in the initial review. The five non-premise SAT queries provide consistency and small countermodel witnesses; they are not universal preservation proofs.
